title: Implement scan_inline_uuencode() utility function
description:
Inline uuencode: UU blocks embedded in text/plain bodies with no CTE header. Decision: option 3 — separate opt-in utility function. parse() is unchanged.

New public function in a new src/uuencode.rs module:

pub struct InlineUUBlock {
    /// Byte offset of the 'begin NNN filename' line within the raw message bytes (from part.body_range.0).
    pub begin_offset: u32,
    /// Byte length from the 'begin' line through the 'end' line (inclusive) within the raw message bytes.
    pub begin_length: u32,
    /// The file permission mode from the begin line (e.g. 644).
    pub mode: u32,
    /// The filename from the begin line, raw (not decoded).
    pub filename: String,
    /// Decoded binary content. Empty if malformed.
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    /// True if any decode error was encountered (malformed line, truncated block, missing end).
    pub is_encoding_problem: bool,
}

pub fn scan_inline_uuencode(raw: &[u8], part: &ParsedPart) -> Vec<InlineUUBlock>

Behavior:
- Slices raw using part.body_range to get the body bytes
- Scans for 'begin NNN filename\n' lines (NNN is octal mode, 3 digits)
- For each begin line found, decodes until 'end\n' or a backtick-only line followed by 'end\n' (the zero-length terminator line is a single backtick)
- Multiple UU blocks in one body are all returned
- Content outside begin/end blocks is ignored (caller already has the full text via decode_body_value)
- Offsets in InlineUUBlock are relative to the start of raw (absolute, same coordinate space as body_range)
- max_bytes: no limit parameter — caller controls what to do with data
- If body_range is out of bounds of raw, returns empty Vec (same defensive pattern as decode_body_value)
- Does NOT call decode_body_value internally; works directly on raw bytes

Documentation requirements (these are MANDATORY — this is the 'document it well' requirement):
- Module-level doc comment explaining what inline uuencode is, why it predates MIME, when it appears in practice, and that this is an opt-in utility distinct from parse()
- Function-level doc comment with: what it does, parameters, return value, example showing a real begin/end block and the call pattern, note that parse() is NOT called and the part tree is NOT modified
- InlineUUBlock doc comments on every field
- A doc-test showing the call pattern (can use a minimal synthetic raw message)

Test oracle: Python uu module. Example:
  import uu, io
  uu.decode(io.BytesIO(b'begin 644 hello.txt\n-2&5L;&\n \nend\n'), io.BytesIO())
Or the UNIX uuencode utility. Do NOT derive expected decoded bytes from this crate.

Acceptance criteria:
- scan_inline_uuencode finds all UU blocks in a body with one block
- scan_inline_uuencode finds all UU blocks in a body with two blocks
- Correct begin_offset and begin_length for each block (verified by slicing raw)
- Correct mode and filename parsed from begin line
- data matches Python uu module output exactly
- Missing 'end' line sets is_encoding_problem=true
- Body with no UU blocks returns empty Vec
- Out-of-bounds body_range returns empty Vec
- Doc-test compiles and passes
